messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Triggered alert `PD: capacity_exhaustion_inference_queue` for service 'inference-core' (severity: P1) — request queue > 95% for 5m in region us-west-2. Link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PABC123

pagerduty: Page fired: PD alert #PABC123 assigned to on-call schedule 'eng-oncall'. Escalation policy: 2m -> 3m -> 5m.

Sam Miller: Acked. I'm taking this.

Priya Patel: Thx Sam. Can you post current customer impact? Any traffic spikes?

Sam Miller: Early look: 10–12% increase on inference requests overall but queue backlog concentrated on model-group 'text-gen-8k'. Pod backpressure visible. Latency tail > 3s for many requests.

Mateo Rodriguez: I'm seeing autoscaler logs showing repeated failures to scale: controller error "provisioner quota exceeded" for shared-pool. Kube API returning 403 for nodegroup creation.

Lin Zhao: Also seeing lots of KV cache evictions on warmup — high cold-start token hits, which is spiking memory. Might be increasing per-request CPU and blocking scaling.

Sam Miller: Good catch Lin. Running quick check against quota: `gcloud compute instance-templates list --filter=...` (private infra) — but quotas look fine last I checked. Mateo, can you paste the controller error lines?

Mateo Rodriguez: Paste from controller logs:

```
E 2026-06-14T18:02:04Z autoscaler-controller: failed to create nodegroup: CloudQuotaExceeded: requested 10, available 0
W 2026-06-14T18:02:06Z autoscaler-controller: retrying backoff=30s
E 2026-06-14T18:04:11Z autoscaler-controller: handshake timeout with provisioner: context deadline exceeded
```

Sam Miller: Ok that's the root cause for scale not happening: provisioner can't allocate instances. Might be cloud provider-side quota or API throttling.

Priya Patel: I've opened a cloud support ticket and requested quota bump / emergency provisioning. Ticket #CLOUD-9981, severity high. Support Oncall, please surface if customers open tickets.

Support Oncall: Roger. I'll watch support queue and post any incoming customer reports here.

Lin Zhao: Quick mitigation idea: can we pivot hot traffic to a lower-memory model variant (text-gen-4k) for a subset of customers? We can change routing policy for the route to fallback to model alias 'text-gen-4k-fast' while we restore capacity.

Sam Miller: Good idea. What's the config change?

Lin Zhao: We can add a routing override in ConfigMap `route-overrides/production` with:

```
route: /v1/generation
policy: prefer(text-gen-8k) -> fallback(text-gen-4k-fast)
criteria: if queue_len > 500 && model == text-gen-8k
```

I can push canary to 5% of traffic to begin.

Mateo Rodriguez: Manual spin-up option: we can provision a small dedicated spare pool from reserved capacity (dedicated) to offload the hot cell. That requires ops approval but is faster than cloud quota resolution in some regions.

Priya Patel: I'm asking finance/ops for immediate approval on reserved burst pool. If granted, how fast?

Sam Miller: If ops approves, we can route 20% traffic in ~6 minutes once instances boot and runtime attaches.

incident-bot: Update: PagerDuty alert #PABC123 acknowledged by Sam Miller at 18:05 UTC.

pagerduty: Escalation canceled (ack received).

Sam Miller: Action plan: 1) apply routing override canary 5% to fallback model (Lin) 2) request reserved burst (Priya) 3) monitor queue and if no improvement escalate to manual node spin-up (Mateo) 4) keep customers updated (Support Oncall).

Lin Zhao: Pushing canary now. Command:

```
kubectl apply -f route-override-canary.yaml --namespace=prod
```

Canary pushed to 5% for /v1/generation.

Sam Miller: Seeing immediate drop in queue for canary subset, CPU/mem per-pod also lower for fallbacks. Nice.

Mateo Rodriguez: Ops approval for dedicated burst: approved. Requested 12 nodes from reserved capacity pool in us-west-2. Provisioner job started.

incident-bot: Provisioner job created: job-id prov-7783. Watching for attach.

Mateo Rodriguez: Provisioner logs show attach succeeded for 6/12 nodes so far. Handshake timeouts earlier were due to control-plane transient errors; it's recovering.

Sam Miller: Queue backlog trending down from 98% to 54% in the last 8 minutes. Latency p50/p95 improving.

Priya Patel: Cloud ticket update: Provider increased API quota and confirmed transient throttle lifted (ticket CLOUD-9981). They recommend we add retry with exponential backoff on handshake.

Lin Zhao: We should also enable a temporary kv-cache warmup policy so new nodes prewarm top prefixes — reduces cold-start churn. I'll add a warmup job to the image prefetcher.

Sam Miller: Go for it. Mateo, once nodes fully attached, will roll traffic back off fallback model?

Mateo Rodriguez: Yes, we'll remove the route override gradually: 20% -> 0% over 10 minutes.

Support Oncall: FYI received two customer tickets reporting increased latency but no data loss. I've replied with status: "mitigations in progress, possible temporary fallback routing for some requests".

incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert #PABC123 status changed to RESOLVED (manual close) by Sam Miller at 18:25 UTC.

Sam Miller: Closing here — summary: cause = provisioner handshake timeouts leading to failed nodegroup creation (cloud API throttle/quota); impact = inference queue backlog, elevated latency for text-gen-8k; mitigation = routing fallback canary + reserved burst nodes + cache warmup + provider quota bump.

Priya Patel: Post-incident action items:
- Mateo: add exponential backoff/retries in provisioner for handshake failures (due: 2026-06-18)
- Lin: implement temporary kv prewarm job and monitor effectiveness (due: 2026-06-16)
- Sam: write short incident postmortem and customer-facing blurb for status page (due: 2026-06-15)
- Priya: follow up with cloud provider for long-term quota increase and runbook update (due: 2026-06-17)

Mateo Rodriguez: I'll open PR for provisioner backoff logic and link here.

Lin Zhao: Adding warmup job now. Will post metrics in 30m.

Support Oncall: I'll draft the customer message and share for review.

Sam Miller: Thanks team. Leaving a note: If anyone sees recurring handshake timeouts, page eng-infra and escalate to provider emergency channel.

Priya Patel: Great work — closing thread after postmortem. :thumbsup:
